title: Types of Classification Error
outcome: By the end, I can construct a confusion matrix with declared axes and name both error types.
scenario: A fictional book-condition checker predicts repair or sound.
given: Use reference rows and prediction columns in order sound,repair. Repair is positive.
Six reference/prediction pairs: sound/sound twice; sound/repair once; repair/sound once; repair/repair twice.

steps.label: Declare axes
steps.detail: Rows: reference sound,repair. Columns: predicted sound,repair.

steps.label: Fill sound row
steps.detail: Two true negatives and one false positive: [2,1].

steps.label: Fill repair row
steps.detail: One false negative and two true positives: [1,2].

explanation: Each case enters one cell according to its reference and predicted label. The off-diagonal cells represent different mistakes: a false alarm on a sound book versus a missed repair. Trace the cell definitions before naming rates; swapping axes changes the table’s interpretation even if its diagonal sum remains unchanged.

counterfactual.change: Change one repair/sound prediction to repair/repair after a real model revision.
counterfactual.reason: One false negative moves to true positive; the sound row stays [2,1].

student_task: Which error causes a sound book to be sent for unnecessary repair review?
teacher_answer: The sound/repair cell is a false positive; there is one in the original matrix.
project_evidence: Use a confusion table when evaluating recommender category predictions and attach concrete consequences to each error.
limits: Reference labels can themselves be disputed; a true-positive name does not guarantee the annotation is infallible.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
